title: BalancerPoolerMintDebtHook.pull() is not gated by NFTMinterV2 global pause; emergency stop does not halt phUSD minting through the hook
description: The hook is a peer to BalancerPoolerV2 in the system-of-record for value flow: debt accrues as USDS is dispatched, and `pull()` materializes that debt as freshly-minted phUSD. However, the hook has no connection to the NFTMinterV2 pauser role or any other emergency-stop control surface. When the NFTMinterV2 pauser role triggers a global pause (src/V2/NFTMinterV2.sol:111-115), new mints via _executeMint are blocked and (per M-01) mintFor remains open. The hook's `pull()` is ALSO unaffected by that global pause: anyone holding the `recipient` role or the hook's owner role can still call `pull()` and mint phUSD during an emergency. Since the BalancerPoolerV2 dispatcher has its own pause (via onlyMinter pause controlled by NFTMinterV2), debt accrual stops during a pause — but the already-accrued ledger remains drainable. For an emergency stop triggered because of a dispatcher-level exploit (e.g. an accounting issue affecting how sUSDS is deposited), the ability to still mint unbacked phUSD via pull() directly undermines the freeze.
impact: Global pause is incomplete: phUSD can continue to be minted via the hook while the rest of the protocol is stopped. The attack surface is bounded by the owner/recipient trust assumption (owner-driven is out of scope per the project's documented known issues), but this specifically concerns the pauser role (a lower-trust emergency-response role). The gap is conceptually identical to M-01 (mintFor bypass of pause) but on a different control surface (phUSD mint via hook, not V2 NFT mint via mintFor).
recommendation: Either (a) add a pauser-controlled kill switch on the hook (e.g., inherit the same pauser pattern as NFTMinterV2, or expose a `setPaused(bool)` gated on a pauser address); or (b) have the hook consult NFTMinterV2.paused() inside `pull()` (requires passing NFTMinterV2 address in the constructor and reading `.paused()`); or (c) document explicitly that phUSD mint-debt is decoupled from protocol pause so downstream integrators can architect their response runbooks accordingly.
